g.text: How turnout changed, weighted by locality size
Change in turnout from the 2022 to the 2026 Knesset election, grouped by how localities voted in 2022, with each locality
weighted by its number of eligible voters in 2022, so large cities count for more than villages.

Coalition: Likud, Religious Zionism, Shas, United Torah Judaism. Opposition: Yesh Atid, National Unity, Yisrael Beiteinu, Labor, Meretz. Balance = (coalition − opposition) ÷ (coalition + opposition) votes, 2022.
Arab-party plurality: Ra'am, Hadash–Ta'al or Balad was the single most-voted list in 2022. Turnout = votes ÷ eligible voters at the locality's ballot boxes (double envelopes excluded).
Sources: Central Elections Committee 2022 final results; CEC 2026 results by locality, all ballot boxes counted (31 Oct 2026, not yet certified). n = 1,215 localities.
Weights: 2022 eligible voters. The CI uses the effective number of localities, (Σw)² ÷ Σw². All localities combined = Σ votes ÷ Σ eligible voters in each year.
